headline_marked: Over 1 million fans join [[Spain's World Cup victory parade]] in Madrid
headline: Over 1 million fans join Spain's World Cup victory parade in Madrid
summary: The champions returned home after defeating Argentina 1-0 in the final, becoming the first country to hold both men's and women's World Cup trophies simultaneously.
details: A jubilant crowd of over a million people flooded the streets of Madrid on Monday to celebrate Spain's second World Cup title. The players traveled on an open-top bus from Moncloa to Cibeles square, where over 120,000 fans had gathered for a final ceremony and concert.

The victory came after Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in extra-time in New Jersey, with Ferran Torres scoring the decisive goal. Upon their return, the team was received by King Felipe VI and Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.
Spain captain Rodri described the win as the crowning achievement of his career, noting that this generation grew up watching previous legends like Iker Casillas and Andres Iniesta.
In a historic milestone, Spain now becomes the first country to hold both the men's and women's World Cup trophies at the same time, following the women's side victory in 2023.
The team will now prepare to defend their crown on home soil in 2030, as Spain is set to co-host the tournament alongside Portugal and Morocco.
On the other side of the triumph, Lionel Messi expressed immense pain on Instagram following Argentina's defeat, stating that the wound would be hard to heal.
caption:
A sea of red and yellow! Over 1 million people hit the streets of Madrid to celebrate Spain's World Cup glory.

A jubilant crowd of over a million people flooded the streets of Madrid on Monday to celebrate Spain's second World Cup title. The players traveled on an open-top bus from Moncloa to Cibeles square, where over 120,000 fans had gathered for a final ceremony and concert.

The victory came after Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in extra-time in New Jersey, with Ferran Torres scoring the decisive goal. Upon their return, the team was received by King Felipe VI and Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.

Spain captain Rodri described the win as the crowning achievement of his career, noting that this generation grew up watching previous legends like Iker Casillas and Andres Iniesta.

In a historic milestone, Spain now becomes the first country to hold both the men's and women's World Cup trophies at the same time, following the women's side victory in 2023.

The team will now prepare to defend their crown on home soil in 2030, as Spain is set to co-host the tournament alongside Portugal and Morocco.

On the other side of the triumph, Lionel Messi expressed immense pain on Instagram following Argentina's defeat, stating that the wound would be hard to heal.

headline_marked: 14 dead this monsoon: [[Rohingya woman killed]] in Ukhiya landslide
headline: 14 dead this monsoon: Rohingya woman killed in Ukhiya landslide
summary: A 19-year-old woman died and a three-year-old child was injured after a hillside collapsed onto a shelter in Rohingya Camp-8 East.
details: A 19-year-old Rohingya woman, Bibi Hafsa, was killed and a three-year-old child, Abdul Majid, was injured after a landslide struck a shelter in Cox's Bazar's Ukhiya on Monday evening.
The incident occurred around 6:30pm in block D/5, sub-block B/77 of Rohingya Camp-8 East, when a portion of a hillside suddenly collapsed onto a shelter built on its slope.
Local volunteers and residents rushed to the scene to rescue victims and other family members who were trapped inside the collapsed shelter.
The injured child was taken to GK Hospital for medical treatment.
According to Atikur Rahman Majumder, officer-in-charge of Ukhiya Police Station, continuous rainfall had loosened the soil on the hillside, triggering the landslide.
This latest tragedy brings the total number of Rohingyas killed in different landslides within the camps during this monsoon season to 14.
caption:

A 19-year-old Rohingya woman, Bibi Hafsa, was killed and a three-year-old child, Abdul Majid, was injured after a landslide struck a shelter in Cox's Bazar's Ukhiya on Monday evening.

The incident occurred around 6:30pm in block D/5, sub-block B/77 of Rohingya Camp-8 East, when a portion of a hillside suddenly collapsed onto a shelter built on its slope.

Local volunteers and residents rushed to the scene to rescue victims and other family members who were trapped inside the collapsed shelter.

The injured child was taken to GK Hospital for medical treatment.

According to Atikur Rahman Majumder, officer-in-charge of Ukhiya Police Station, continuous rainfall had loosened the soil on the hillside, triggering the landslide.

This latest tragedy brings the total number of Rohingyas killed in different landslides within the camps during this monsoon season to 14.
